_dns_note: OPTIONAL, and you almost certainly want the default. Boxes get PINNED DNS servers (default 8.8.8.8 + 8.8.4.4, Docker's own public fallbacks) instead of inheriting the host's resolver state. Reason: a container's /etc/resolv.conf is written ONCE at start and never revisited, so a host that doesn't know its nameservers yet in that instant cripples the box permanently — and a box joined to a repo's host_stack network gets Docker's embedded resolver with the host's upstreams as forwarders, which with no upstreams to copy means NO forwarders at all: container names resolve, every public name SERVFAILs, and claude reports `OAuth error: getaddrinfo ESERVFAIL platform.claude.com` with no Remote Control until the container is recreated. Set "dns" (a list, or one string) only if these servers are wrong for your network — an internal resolver, a filtered upstream. Service-name resolution inside a host_stack network is unaffected either way.

host.name: host
host._note: OPTIONAL. Only for `gent host …` — a claude you run ON this machine (not in a box) and reach from your phone. Boxes don't need this. `name` is the tmux session + display name (pick anything). `gent host up` runs it under a self-healing supervisor AND arms a launchd keepalive job (one command) so an IDLE session re-mints its token before expiry and never drops Remote Control. Requires tmux on the host (`brew install tmux`).

_comment: Copy this file to fleet.json and edit — fleet.json is gitignored (it's your machine's private grants). state_root (~/.gent/state) is the single relocatable home for precious, non-git fleet state: secrets/ (a shared CATALOG of reusable credential files + .env fragments, referenced by relative path — isolation happens in the grant, so a box sees only what its entry lists and can never get more) and app/<box>/ (per-box app state pulled out of volumes/repos, bound read-write via a repo's `state_mounts`). secrets_root defaults to state_root/secrets. projects_root is where your repos live; each repo's `path` is relative to it.

myapp._note: `allow` is the trust gate — gent refuses to start a box whose entry isn't allow:true. This example grants a scoped GCP service-account key (mounted read-only), a shared .env fragment, a read-only per-owner GitHub token (so in-box `gh` can read PRs/diffs/CI — see README), a Vercel token (so in-box `vercel` can deploy / push prod env — the CLI auto-reads VERCEL_TOKEN; VERCEL_SCOPE pins the team — use the team ID `team_…` from .vercel/project.json's orgId, not the slug, since a slug that collides with your personal username resolves to your empty personal account), and some inline ids. NOTE a Vercel token is full-access within its team (Pro can't scope it to one project), so mint it deliberately and revoke to rotate.
myapp._data_mounts_note: OPTIONAL. Plain host data the box may read but never owns — absolute or ~ host paths, always mounted READ-ONLY (e.g. a large dataset kept out of git). Not for credentials (use `mounts`, from the catalog) or app state the box writes (use `state_mounts`). A missing source path refuses to start the box rather than mounting an empty dir.

closed_windows.why: morning weigh-ins: 14 of 32 readings. Ends at 11:00, not 10:30, because the latest morning reading on record is 10:50.
evening weigh-ins: 14 of 32, 11 at 22:00 alone. Crosses midnight-ish deliberately: the latest is 23:35.

restart-scale.closed_basis: counted from the scale ledger 2026-09-12: n=32 over 15 days, and these blocks cover all 32. The open hours being empty is an ABSENCE claim — re-measure as the habit moves.

myapp._host_actions_note: OPTIONAL, and a real grant of power — read this before adding one. A box has no docker socket (it runs claude with permissions skipped; the socket is root on the host), but a box often CANNOT restart the very process holding its code: an api container that mounts the repo read-only keeps its modules in memory, so an edit is dormant, silently, until someone on the host restarts it. Each entry gives the box ONE NAME it may ask for; the argv lives here, on the host, and the box can never compose a command, pass an argument, or name a service you didn't list. gent binds a spool at /gent/host-actions (also $GENT_HOST_ACTIONS) for boxes that declare this, and `gent fleet timers install` arms the 30 s runner that serves it. Shorthand: a bare argv list instead of the object, when the action needs no guards. `min_interval_s` stops a caller that watches a signal from restarting in a loop when the signal doesn't clear — the second ask inside the window is REFUSED, with a reason, never silently dropped. `group` + `group_cooldown_s` keep actions that share a physical resource apart (two BLE sidecars on one radio: restarted together, the second blocks past its radio lock and sits in `starting` for fifteen minutes) — a grouped ask that arrives too early is DEFERRED and retried, not refused. `closed_windows` (+ optional `tz`, per-window `why`, action-level `closed_basis`) is the third guard and the only one about PEOPLE rather than the machine: hours in which the action is REFUSED, because no signal inside the box can tell you that restarting the scale at 22:00 costs the weighing someone is standing on. Refused, not deferred — a cooldown is seconds, a window is hours, and a queued request would fire unattended long after the asker's session ended. It fails CLOSED: a window that doesn't parse refuses the ask rather than reading as no guard. Make the window state its own evidence — a bare pair of times is a rule nobody can re-check, and a deadline chosen by feel once expired into the single most common weighing hour on record. Keep the vocabulary tiny: every action is a line a human wrote here, and the point is that you can read a box's whole reach in ten seconds.

minimal._note: Simplest case: a repo in its own box, no secrets, no env.
